newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 11.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A new group has been formed that will push for a second term for President Fidel Ramos. (INQUIRER)
- The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) announced it had postponed Cambodia's membership but would still admit Burma and Laos later this month. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The problem of Cambodia will be a test of leadership for the Philippines once Manila assumes chairmanship of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) Standing Commitee at the end of the ministerial meeting this month. (MANILA TIMES)
- Metro Manila traffic authorities will start on July 21 the implementation of the odd-even scheme for motorists aimed at decongesting traffic. (MANILA STANDARD)

- Executive Secretary Ruben Torres said Thursday night that the Monetary Board, the policy-making arm of the Central Bank, will be asked to refrain from its costly intervention in the currency market and instead allow the peso to seek its value against the US dollar. The Monetary Board is expected to announce major changes in the country's foreign exchange policy today. (BUSINESSWORLD/MALAYA)

- The Central Bank on Thursday raised its overnight rates by two percentage points to defend the peso from speculators but appeared helpless to prevent a peso-linked fresh slump in the stock market. The stock market main index fell to a two-month low, closing 78.05 points, or 3.01 percent, at 2,511.15. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The Central Bank may use its weapons to defend the peso but the gross international reserves (GIR) are dwindling fast. (MANILA TIMES)

- Foreign mining firms said bureaucratic red tape in the issuance of exploration permits could deprive the Philippines of substantial foreign investments which may instead flow to other countries. (MANILA BULLETIN)
